newsitem.title: MEXICO: BASEBALL-DOMINICAN REPUBLIC TAKES CARIBBEAN TITLE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-DOMINICAN REPUBLIC TAKES CARIBBEAN TITLE.

text.p: The Dominican Republic's Cibao Eagles were down and nearly out after the first two games of the Caribbean Series of baseball, their hitters not hitting and their pitchers getting rocked by opposing batters.
But two games later in the tournament of professional winter league champions from four Latin American countries, all four teams were tied at 2-2, and by then the Dominicans had their game together.

On Sunday, they were crowned champions of the 27th annual Caribbean Series by defeating Mexico's Culiacan Tomato Growers 4-3 for their fourth straight victory before a sellout and mostly Mexican crowd of 15,500 at Hermosillo's Hector Espino Stadium.

"We've won four in a row before but when you're under these kind of circumstances where it's basically a single-elimination deal after the first two games, it's the greatest feeling in the world," Dominican manager Mike Quade said after the game.

At the same time, the Mexican players were proud of their performance after coming into the series with only one Major League Baseball player while other teams had as many as 13. The Culiacan team was the surprise champion a year ago in the Dominican Republic.

"It would have been better to complete another championship, but it was tough," said Mexican manager Francisco Estrada, who was voted the best manager in the series by the media. "This was a good experience for the people who never believe in Mexico. We're having a party."
The Dominican Republic finished 4-2, Mexico 3-3, Venezuela's Magellan Navigators 3-3 and Puerto Rico's Mayaguez Indians 2-4.
The Dominican bats' return to life was led by second baseman and cleanup hitter Tony Bautista, who finished the tournament with a .384 average, two homers and a Series-leading 13 runs batted in.
"We weren't expecting this much pitching in the first two games," Bautista said, explaining the early Dominican slump.

His three-run homer off Mexican starter Martin Hernandez in the first inning set the tone for the rest of Sunday's game. He next heads to the Oakland A's major-league spring training camp, where he will compete for the starting job at second base.

Dominican catcher Guillermo Garcia, who also plays in the Cincinnati Reds organisation, hit .348 with three homers and eight RBIs, including what proved to be the game-winner with a sixth-inning sacrifice fly to score the fourth run.

But the Most Valuable Player of the Series, voted by the media, was Mexican designated hitter Matt Stark, a former major-league catcher who hit four mammoth home runs, each one at a crucial time, to give Mexico a fighting chance.
"I'm disappointed because I thought that we beat ourselves tonight. We had a chance to win the game," Stark said just before picking up his MVP trophy.

The fourth Dominican run was unearned because a throwing error by third baseman Oscar Romero allowed the runner to advance a base, and later a base-running error by Mexico's Darryl Brinkely cut short a rally.

Down 4-0, Mexico mounted a threat in the top of the seventh when it scored a run on Brinkley's RBI single to put runners at the corners. On the next play, Adan Amezcua, the runner at third base, was thrown out at the plate on an infield grounder.
Brinkley was the third out in the inning when he tried an ill-advised steal of home and got caught in a rundown.
